{{nihongo|'''Namura Shrine'''|苗村神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Namura Shrine''' (なむらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Ryūō, Shiga|arz|ريو|ceb|Ryūō-chō|es|Ryūō (Shiga)|fa|ریوئو، شیگا|fr|Ryūō|hu|Rjúó|hy|Ռյուո|id|Ryūō, Shiga|it|Ryūō|ja|竜王町|ko|류오정|ms|Ryūō, Shiga|pl|Ryūō|ru|Рюо|sv|Ryūō, Shiga|tl|Ryūō, Shiga|tr|Ryūō|uk|Рюо|ur|ریو، شیگا|vi|Ryūō, Shiga|zh|龍王町|qid=Q1087560}}, {{ill|Gamō District, Shiga|ceb|Gamō-gun|es|Distrito de Gamō (Shiga)|fa|شهرستان گامو، شیگا|fr|District de Gamō|hu|Gamó körzet|id|Distrik Gamō, Shiga|it|Distretto di Gamō|ja|蒲生郡|ko|가모군 (시가현)|ms|Daerah Gamō, Shiga|pl|Powiat Gamō|ru|Гамо|zh|蒲生郡|qid=Q931658}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is a high-ranking {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} as Nagamura (Namura) Shrine. Under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank system}}, it was a {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}. It is the head shrine for parishioners across 33 nearby villages.

=== History ===
Its detailed foundation is unknown, but shrine tradition says it began as an ancestral-spirit cult in the era of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}. At the site of the Higashi-Namura Kofun group, a shrine called Nagamura ("naga" as highest rank and "mura" as an old character for village), phonetically matching Namura, was established; this is the present East Main Hall.

In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, it was listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} and ranked as a Shikinaisha.

On March 28, {{ill|Anna (era)|Q1373003|qid=Q1373003}} 2 ({{ill|969|Q23708|qid=Q23708}}), the divine spirit of Kunikuzuchi-no-Mikoto from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kinpusen}} in {{ill|Yoshino|Q15410122|qid=Q15410122}} of {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} was enshrined west of the sacred precinct, and a new shrine building was constructed. This shrine came to be called the West Main Hall in contrast to the previous main hall (East Main Hall).

In the first month of {{ill|Kannin|Q1193951|qid=Q1193951}} 1 ({{ill|1017|Q19249|qid=Q19249}}), after presenting young pine trees for the imperial New Year gate decorations ({{ill|Kadomatsu|Q2667233|qid=Q2667233}}) to the {{ill|Imperial Court of Japan|Q30253177|qid=Q30253177|lt=court}}, it became an annual custom; then {{ill|Emperor Go-Ichijō|Q374087|qid=Q374087}} bestowed the title Namura, and it came to be called Namura.

On March 2, {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 5 ({{ill|1536|Q6457|qid=Q6457}}), it received the divine rank of "Senior First Rank" from {{ill|Emperor Go-Nara|Q349467|qid=Q349467}}. On April 9 of the same year, envoy {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nakanomikado Munefuji}} and {{ill|Yamashina Tokitsugu|Q11470822|qid=Q11470822}} dedicated the written record of divine rank. On May 9, the imperial plaque "Senior First Rank Namura Daimyojin" was also bestowed.

During the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}-{{ill|1593|Q6772|qid=Q6772}}), {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} donated a full horse harness and seven swords.

In {{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 14) it became a gosha, and in {{ill|1920|Q2155|qid=Q2155}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 9) it was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Main deities - {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Namurahiko-no-kami}} (なむらひこがみ), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Namurahime-no-kami}} (なむらひめがみ), and {{ill|Kunisatsuchi-no-Mikoto|Q5966692|qid=Q5966692}} (くにのさづちのみこと); deities of the West Main Hall.
* Deities in the shared hall - {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}} (おおくにぬしのみこと), {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-kami}} (ことしろぬしのかみ), and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} (すさのおのみこと); deities of the East Main Hall.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== National Treasure ===
* West Main Hall, plus: one zushi shrine cabinet and one munafuda board

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* East Main Hall, plus: two munafuda boards
* Main hall of Hachiman Shrine
* Main hall of Jūzenji Shrine
* Rōmon gate, plus: two old timbers
* Shinko storehouse
* Wooden standing statue of {{ill|Acala|Q337624|qid=Q337624}}

=== Festivals ===
;Namura Festival
An ancient grand festival held every year on April 20. With a sacred horse procession from nine {{ill|miyaza|Q11454763|qid=Q11454763}} seats, after dedication rites ten sacred horses and three portable shrines proceed in line and make a procession to the resting place.
;Sekku Festival
A grand festival on May 5 celebrating children's growth. Child mikoshi dedication and ten sacred horses run along the approach in traditional costume in the dynamic "{{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157|lt=ryūsenma}}" event, attracting many visitors all day.
;Shikinen Festival (33-year grand festival)
{{要出典範囲|date=2017年5月|Formerly, a grand festival with participation from 33 parish villages was held every year on September 5.}} Since {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 4 ({{ill|1599|Q6803|qid=Q6803}}), it has been held once every 33 years<ref name="chunichi2016323">{{Cite news ja | title = Once every 33 years: Ryuo, Namura Shrine Grand Festival; prefectural university survey team publishes record book | newspaper = {{ill|Chunichi Shimbun|Q904678|qid=Q904678}} | date = 2016-03-23 | author = Kanako Kawabe | publisher = Chunichi Shimbun Co. | edition= morning, Biwako edition |page=24 }}</ref>. The 2014 event (Heisei 26) is said to have been the 14th.

=== Blessings ===
* Matchmaking
* Prosperous business / success and good fortune, abundant harvests
* Safe childbirth and children
* Protection from misfortune
